name: Frankfurt am Main
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Frankfurt am Main: financial sector due diligence, AML-related inquiries and commercial court support.
hero_lede: Investigative consulting for matters that run through Frankfurt: banks, asset managers and fintechs in continental Europe's main supervisory centre, disputes before the new English-language commercial court and chambers, and transactions financed or listed in the city. Scoped from Nashville with qualified German professionals.
intro: Frankfurt am Main is Germany's financial capital and one of the principal regulatory centres of the European Union. The European Central Bank, the Deutsche Bundesbank, the German Federal Financial Supervisory Authority (BaFin) and the European Insurance and Occupational Pensions Authority are based in the city, and in February 2024 the EU chose Frankfurt as headquarters of its new Anti-Money Laundering Authority (AMLA). The Frankfurt Stock Exchange, major German and international banks, asset managers, payment and fintech companies, law and audit firms, and one of Europe's busiest airports and logistics hubs make the city a focal point for finance, trade and professional services in the state of Hesse.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Frankfurt because capital, credit and compliance risk converge there. Typical triggers include due diligence on banks, payment institutions, crypto-asset service providers and fund managers ahead of transactions or partnerships; background research on senior managers and controlling shareholders; support to counsel in post-acquisition, shareholder and financing disputes, which since July 2025 can be brought before English-language commercial panels in Frankfurt; and inquiries into suspected fraud, market abuse or money laundering exposure in financial institutions. Asset tracing for enforcement, and research on counterparties in air cargo, logistics and trade finance flowing through the Rhine-Main region, are also common.

matters.title: Financial institution counterparty due diligence
matters.text: Ownership, management and regulatory history of banks, payment institutions, crypto-asset providers and fund managers based in Frankfurt, drawing on commercial register filings, published financial statements, supervisory announcements and media, to support acquisitions, correspondent relationships, partnerships and outsourcing decisions.

matters.title: Commercial court dispute support
matters.text: Fact development, background on parties and witnesses, and document chronology work for M&A, corporate and business-to-business disputes before the Frankfurt Commercial Court or Commercial Chambers, structured with German counsel so that findings can be used in English-language proceedings.

matters.title: AML and financial crime inquiries
matters.text: Support to counsel and compliance teams reviewing suspected money laundering, sanctions evasion or fraud exposure involving Frankfurt institutions or their clients, focusing on ownership chains, source-of-wealth indicators and adverse public records rather than any access to restricted supervisory data.

matters.title: Executive and shareholder background research
matters.text: Lawful background research on proposed directors, key function holders and qualifying shareholders of Frankfurt financial firms, covering directorships, insolvency and court records, sanctions exposure and reputation, to help clients anticipate fit-and-proper scrutiny and manage governance risk.

matters.title: Logistics and trade finance exposure
matters.text: Research on freight forwarders, air cargo intermediaries and trading companies operating around Frankfurt Airport and the Rhine-Main region, where trade finance, documentary fraud and export control issues can arise, supporting lenders, insurers and counsel investigating losses or suspicious transactions.

local_context.title: Frankfurt Commercial Court and Chambers
local_context.text: Under Germany's Commercial Courts Act, Hesse opened a Commercial Court at the Higher Regional Court Frankfurt am Main and Commercial Chambers at the Regional Court Frankfurt on 1 July 2025. According to the Hessian Ministry of Justice, they take business-to-business, corporate and company or share acquisition disputes with a value of at least 500,000 euros, can conduct proceedings in English and offer protection for trade secrets. Several categories, including insurance and insolvency matters, are excluded.

local_context.title: Courts and commercial register
local_context.text: Frankfurt's Regional Court is one of Germany's busiest for commercial and banking litigation, and the Higher Regional Court Frankfurt hears appeals from across much of Hesse. The commercial register for companies seated in the city is kept by the Local Court Frankfurt am Main and is searchable through the joint register portal of the German states described on the Germany country page.

local_context.title: European and German supervisors
local_context.text: The ECB, Bundesbank, BaFin and EIOPA are based in Frankfurt, and the EU selected the city as seat of AMLA on 22 February 2024. Their published decisions, sanctions, registers of authorised institutions and warnings about unauthorised firms are important lawful sources in due diligence. Supervisory files and suspicious activity reports are confidential and are not accessible to investigators.

local_context.title: Hesse data protection supervision
local_context.text: Germany's federal data protection rules apply nationwide, but supervision of most private-sector processing is carried out at state level. For organisations established in Frankfurt this is the Hessian Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information, based in Wiesbaden. Investigative work involving employees or customers of Frankfurt entities should be planned with that authority's guidance and the employer's works council arrangements in mind.

tdsc_approach: For matters touching Frankfurt, TDSC first identifies the regulatory perimeter of the entities involved, since banks, payment firms and fund managers sit under ECB, BaFin or, increasingly, EU-level AML supervision, and that shapes what records exist and what is confidential. Research relies on the commercial register, published accounts, supervisory registers and decisions, court records and open sources, reviewed under the GDPR and German data protection law. For disputes, TDSC aligns work with German counsel and with the forum, including the English-language Frankfurt Commercial Court where it applies. Where interviews or fieldwork in Frankfurt are needed, TDSC coordinates German investigators operating under the applicable trade rules. TDSC has no office in Frankfurt.

faqs.q: Can disputes in Frankfurt now be heard in English?
faqs.a: Yes, in qualifying cases. Since 1 July 2025 the Frankfurt Commercial Court at the Higher Regional Court and the Commercial Chambers at the Regional Court can conduct proceedings in English for business, corporate and M&A disputes of at least 500,000 euros, subject to exclusions. Counsel decides whether a case qualifies; TDSC tailors its reporting accordingly.

faqs.q: Can TDSC obtain information from BaFin or the ECB about an institution?
faqs.a: No. Supervisory files are confidential. TDSC uses what these authorities publish, such as registers of authorised firms, sanctions announcements and warnings about unauthorised business, alongside commercial register filings, accounts and court records. Any request for non-public information is a matter for the client's counsel and the authority concerned.

faqs.q: What does AMLA's seat in Frankfurt mean for investigations?
faqs.a: AMLA, the EU Anti-Money Laundering Authority headquartered in Frankfurt, is building EU-level supervision of anti-money laundering compliance in the financial sector. For clients this raises expectations on ownership transparency and source-of-funds checks for counterparties, which TDSC addresses through lawful ownership and reputation research rather than access to supervisory data.

faqs.q: Which data protection authority is relevant to a Frankfurt employer?
faqs.a: Private-sector data processing by organisations established in Frankfurt is generally supervised by the Hessian Commissioner for Data Protection and Freedom of Information. Internal investigations should be planned with counsel, the data protection officer and, where applicable, the works council, and TDSC limits personal data gathered to what the agreed purpose requires.

faqs.q: Does TDSC have staff in Frankfurt?
faqs.a: No. TDSC has no office, staff or address in Frankfurt or elsewhere in Germany. Engagements are scoped and managed from Nashville. Where a matter requires local inquiries, TDSC coordinates independent German investigators and works with the client's German counsel, within a written scope agreed before work starts.
